notes: Extracted 29 October 2026 from the guide (src/guides/arealinechart.guide.tsx and src/AreaLineChartGuide.tsx) and docs/evidence/arealinechart.md at 4e470cf. The guide was built by Codex on 22 September from jfs-components 0.1.60; its Sources note was re-checked on 1 October 2026 on 0.1.78 (mirror v0.1.78, built from 5b6894b, the #166 fix), and the evidence's 0.1.78 check was run the same day on the same build, so items citing either carry that build. The evidence's Batch check (22 September, 0.1.60) is not cited: everything it says that this entry needs is restated by the 0.1.78 check or the Sources note. Installed build: jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (Biscuit's main at dbe0e02, 27 October). Its AreaLineChart.tsx and chartMath.ts still match every guide sentence used here, read from source, not run: an in-flow probe sizes the Y-axis column to its widest tick label; the goal pin's 32 px bubble is clamped inside the plot; height is the plot only, with the x-axis row below it; the y ticks come from a nice-tick helper over the data (from 0 when every value is positive) unless yMin or yMax is given; the line segment ending at a projected point is dashed; the x-axis labels are Pressables that select their point (pressing the active label clears it) and update onActiveIndexChange; on the web hovering the plot selects the nearest point and leaving it clears the selection; the legend shows only with more than one series; series colours come from the Appearance / DataViz cycle (Primary, Secondary, …) unless a series sets its own. Not contradicted, but worth knowing and not recorded as guidance because no source states it: a supplied yMin or yMax is itself rounded out to a nice tick (yMax 725 with four ticks draws the axis to 800), so a bound is not an exact axis end. The 0.1.78 check's last-x-label overflow still follows from the source on dbe0e02 (the last point sits 8 px from the plot's right edge and its label is centred on it), so it is kept as a gap. Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode, and no Appearance / DataViz or Emphasis / DataViz modes (the guide sets Light, Primary and High on every chart, and Primary and High are the defaults); series leave appearance to the default cycle (the guide's Primary and Secondary are the cycle's first two); no style (the guide's width 100% is the container's default) and no interactive (on by default). They keep the guide's data, labels, heights and the k unit through formatY. The In context Card drops the guide's Neutral AppearanceBrand and Light Color Mode, which the guide doesn't explain. The projected example writes the observed points as bare numbers: the guide's x strings are ignored by the package, which places points by index and labels them from xLabels. Left out of examples: the guide's readout line (“Select an x-axis point to inspect its values.”) and its “View plotted values” table, both page HTML rather than Coin; the Don't specimens (mixed units, a hidden legend, long labels); the playground. Not recorded: the composable parts (AreaLineChart.Grid, .XAxis, .YAxis, .GoalPin) and children, which the guide doesn't use or describe; numberOfTicks, contentInset, showXAxis, showYAxis and disableTruncation, which it doesn't mention; per-series colour overrides, which the building rules keep off Coin components. Content bad is the guide's long Don't labels; good is its short labels and series names.

accessibility.text: On the web the x-axis labels are pressable and keyboard reachable, so a point can be selected without a pointer; the rendered accessibility tree does not expose the full series labels, so keep the values available in text when SVG interaction is not enough for the task.

from.quote: SVG interaction is keyboard reachable through the public x-axis Pressable in RN Web, but the rendered accessibility tree does not expose full series labels

examples.purpose: An account balance trend, the guide's In context: a Card gives the account label and the unit context, and the chart plots three months of balance with a goal pin on the last point. The guide also keeps the plotted values in a text table beside it; that table is page HTML, not Coin.
examples.jsx:
<Card>
  <Card.Title>Account balance</Card.Title>
  <Card.SupportText>Direction over the last three months</Card.SupportText>
  <AreaLineChart
    series={[{ key: 'balance', label: 'Balance', data: [620, 590, 725] }]}
    xLabels={['Apr', 'May', 'Jun']}
    height={168}
    goalPin={{ value: '725k', atIndex: 2 }}
    formatY={(value) => `${value}k`}
    accessibilityLabel="Account balance"
  />
</Card>

from.quote: A Card can provide the account label and unit context while the chart stays responsible for the plotted data.

examples.purpose: Series comparison with a point selected, the guide's States: income and spending in the same unit over six months, so two series get the legend automatically. The screen keeps the active index, and the chart shows that point's series values (here February, Income 14k and Spending 8k); pressing an x-axis label or the plot reports the new index through onActiveIndexChange. With no activeIndex the plot stays quiet.
examples.jsx:
<AreaLineChart
  series={[
    { key: 'income', label: 'Income', data: [1, 14, 12, 22, 33, 45] },
    { key: 'spending', label: 'Spending', data: [1, 8, 9, 14, 22, 30] },
  ]}
  xLabels={['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun']}
  showDots
  activeIndex={1}
  onActiveIndexChange={() => {}}
  formatY={(value) => `${value}k`}
/>

from.quote: Expose a selected point and its readable series values.

examples.purpose: A projected tail: three observed months and two projected ones, marked projected in the data so their segments are dashed; the guide turns the area off and shows dots for this one.

<AreaLineChart

      key: 'balance',
      label: 'Balance',
      showArea: false,

    },
  ]}
  xLabels={['Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug']}
  showDots

/>
